claims.text: A hybrid TOR-TILD and machine-learning-potential approach can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The target materials are multicomponent high-entropy alloys initially in the solid state.
The proposed method combines TOR-TILD with machine learning potentials trained using ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
The proposed operating temperature range is 500–2000 K.
The proposed composition domain contains three to six principal elements.
Vibrational entropy is retained as a relevant thermodynamic contribution in the hybrid calculation.
Anharmonicity is retained as a relevant thermodynamic contribution in the hybrid calculation.
Electron–vibration coupling is retained in the hybrid calculation.
TOR-TILD provides accurate results for elemental and binary systems.
Machine learning potentials provide computational efficiency for multicomponent systems.
The hybrid method will reduce computational cost by a factor of 5–10 relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The hybrid method will reduce computational cost by a factor of 2–5 relative to TOR-TILD.
The hybrid method will achieve 90–95% fidelity in predicted phase free energies and derived observables.
The upper temperature boundary is 2000 K.
The upper compositional-complexity boundary is six principal elements.
The accuracy of the hybrid method may depend on the quality of its training set.
The accuracy of the hybrid method may depend on the complexity of the multicomponent system.
The proposed benchmark compares hybrid and explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics phase free energies, entropy, and heat capacity for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis is falsified if the mean absolute error relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics exceeds 10% for phase free energies and derived observables.
